_meta: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED (wired automatically by the gen-slices auto-loader). Continuing municipal-fiscal-tier research, 2026-08-13 (AF/G.23). Gambia (existing corpus: af-gambia.json — gm-gbos-cpi, gm-local-government-act-2002). This round's key discovery: a 'Local Government Finance and Audit Act, 2004' (anticipated by s.130 of the 2002 Act) genuinely exists and is cited by name in two independent primary Gambian government sources (National Audit Office and Kanifing Municipal Council itself), but its full text could not be located online anywhere despite exhaustive search — so no node was minted for the Act itself. Two genuine named-council fiscal documents were minted instead: NAO's own audited financial statements for Kanifing Municipal Council (OCR-extracted from a scanned-image-only PDF — no embedded text layer) and Kanifing Municipal Council's own self-published Budget 2021 Summary (with a quantified 13%-of-revenue Government Subvention figure).

reports.title: Auditor General's Report on Kanifing Municipal Council Financial Statements (Period Ended 1 April 2017 to 31 December 2019)
reports.description: The National Audit Office (Gambia)'s Auditor-General's report on Kanifing Municipal Council's financial statements for the period 1 April 2017 to 31 December 2019, transmitted 3 December 2020 (Ref: HC 93/475/01/PART IV(11), signed by Bakary Trawally, For: Auditor General, copied to the Permanent Secretaries of the Ministry of Local Government and Lands and the Ministry of Finance). States KMC's governing accountability framework: "Management is responsible for the preparation and fair presentation of these financial statements in accordance with Local Government Finance and Audit Act, 2004, Financial and Accounting Manual For Local Government Authorities Chapter 9 on cash basis, and for such internal control as management determines is necessary..." — the first of two independent primary confirmations found this round that a distinct "Local Government Finance and Audit Act, 2004" exists and governs municipal financial accountability, the law anticipated (but not enacted) by the 2002 Local Government Act's own Section 130: "The financial affairs of a Council shall be regulated in accordance with a Local Government (Finance and Audit) law to be enacted by the National Assembly." A companion passage names the fuller compliance stack: financial statements must comply "with the provisions of the Government Budget Management and Accountability Act, Financial and Accounting Manual for Local Government Authorities, Local Government Act, and the Finance and Audit Act." The audited Revenue and Expenditure Statement for FY2019 (with FY2018 comparatives) records Total Revenue of D180,415,062 (2019) vs D142,473,020 (2018), broken into Licences, Taxes, Rents & Fees, Rates, Other Income, and Interest and Dividend; Note 5 ("Other Income") itemizes a "Grants And Subventions - Government" line of D500,000.00 for 2019 versus D2,317,300.00 for 2018 — a documented, audited, named-council-specific central-government transfer figure, though the year-on-year decline is stark. CAVEAT (OCR): the source PDF has no embedded text layer (pdftotext returned zero characters; it is a set of 150dpi scanned-image pages per pdfimages) — all quotes above were extracted via local OCR (tesseract) rather than standard text extraction, and should be treated as OCR-derived, not directly machine-extracted, text. CAVEAT (audit opinion): NAO issued an overall Adverse Opinion on KMC's FY2019 financial statements due to unrelated unexplained balances (accumulated funds, suspense account, etc.), so the underlying financials should be treated as officially contested/unreliable in aggregate even though the specific quoted lines are as NAO itself published them.

reports.title: Kanifing Municipal Council — Budget 2021 Summary
reports.description: Kanifing Municipal Council's own self-published budget page states its statutory basis: "The Kanifing Municipal Council produces an annual budget to manage the financial resources of the Council. In line with the Local Government Finance and Audit Act 2004, the Council has the right and obligation to formulate, approve and execute a financial budget" — a second, fully independent primary confirmation (alongside gm-nao-audit-kmc-2017-2019) that the Local Government Finance and Audit Act, 2004 exists and governs council budgeting, though its full text could not be located online anywhere this round. The page's 'Budget 2021 Summary' section gives KMC's own FY2021 revenue/expenditure figures: "The revenue projected for the fiscal year 2021 amounts to D 280,429,161.15... representing an increase of 30.77% compared to the 2020 budget. The projected revenue comprises of Trade License, Administration income, Markets income, Property Rates, Property Leasing, and Government Subvention... distributed among the revenue earning units as follows: Administration 1%, Market 20%, License 30%, Rates and Taxes 35%, Government Subventions 13%, and Car Park fees 1%" — a specific, named-council, self-reported figure showing central-government subvention as 13% of projected FY2021 revenue. Expenditure: "The projected expenditure for 2021 amounts to D 260,258,993.29... D 92,142,348.69 (35.4%) represents the Recurrent expenditures... while D 168,116,644.60 (64.6%) goes to Development expenditures." CAVEAT (currency of content): the page's schema.org metadata shows dateModified 2023-03-09, but the retrievable body text still only covers 'Budget 2021 Summary' — a referenced 'Budget 2023 Summary' section (page 2 of the paginated post) returned HTTP 200 but rendered no article body (likely requires JS execution), so treat any later-year figures as not-yet-retrieved rather than confirmed absent. CAVEAT (access): this host (kanifing.gm) returned HTTP 403 to a bare/minimal User-Agent or HEAD request during this round's research — successful fetch required a full desktop-browser User-Agent string; treat as bot-gated if re-fetching.
reports.cadence_note: KMC's own site states it produces an annual budget; only the 'Budget 2021 Summary' content was retrievable this round.

dependencies.basis: The audit report's own 'General Council's Responsibilities' passage lists financial-statement compliance obligations including "...Financial and Accounting Manual for Local Government Authorities, Local Government Act, and the Finance and Audit Act..." — a direct, if generic (no section number), textual citation of the 2002 Local Government Act as part of KMC's compliance framework, alongside the separately-named (and still full-text-unlocated) Finance and Audit Act 2004.

No node minted for the Act itself; both citing nodes' descriptions record the confirmed-existence/no-full-text status.
